course: Introduction to the Internet of Things
topic_title: Software-Defined Networking (SDN) for IoT & Mobile Environments

analysis_of_assignment_style.evaluation_depth: Combination of direct factual recall, component identification, protocol/standard matching, and scenario-based application reasoning.

Medium/Hard (Multi-concept synthesis, scenario reasoning, boundary conditions)

topics.description: Control/data plane decoupling, OpenFlow protocol, flow tables, and soft/hard timeouts.

questions.question: What is Software-Defined Networking (SDN)?

options.A: A networking paradigm that decouples the control plane from the data plane, centralizing network intelligence in a software controller
options.B: A method of soldering physical copper wires

questions.justification: SDN separates network control logic (control plane) from underlying packet forwarding hardware (data plane).

questions.question: In SDN-IoT architecture, where are flow classification and enhanced security typically handled as evaluated in Week 8 Question 15?

options.A: At the Data Center Networks / SDN Controller

questions.justification: Flow classification and security policies are centrally managed at the Data Center / SDN Controller level.

questions.question: Which protocol is the standard interface used for communication between the SDN Controller (control plane) and network switches (data plane)?

options.A: OpenFlow

questions.justification: OpenFlow is the standardized southbound protocol connecting SDN controllers to switches.

questions.question: True or False: SDN and OpenFlow are identical terms.

options.A: False (SDN is the overall concept/architecture; OpenFlow is a specific southbound protocol)

questions.justification: SDN is the broader architectural concept; OpenFlow is a specific protocol communicating between control and data planes.

questions.question: Which open-source software switch is the most popular OpenFlow-enabled virtual switch used in SDN deployments?

options.A: Open vSwitch (OVS)

questions.justification: Open vSwitch is the most widely deployed open-source software switch for SDN.

questions.question: How does SDN solve rigid scaling and high operational costs in traditional mobile networks?

options.A: By abstracting physical network hardware into programmable software flows managed by a centralized controller
options.B: By replacing digital signals with analog audio

questions.justification: SDN abstracts rigid hardware into dynamic, software-programmable flow tables.

questions.question: In OpenFlow flow-table management, what is the difference between 'Hard Timeout' and 'Soft Timeout' (Week 7 slides)?

options.A: Hard timeout deletes the rule after a fixed time regardless of activity; Soft timeout deletes the rule only if no matching traffic is received for a specified idle duration
options.B: Hard timeout reboots the switch; Soft timeout reboots the server
options.C: Soft timeout increases voltage; Hard timeout cuts power

questions.justification: Hard timeout forces rule deletion after a fixed duration; Soft timeout deletes idle rules after an inactivity period.

questions.question: What components comprise a standard OpenFlow Flow Table entry inside an SDN switch?

options.A: Match Fields (headers), Counters, and Actions (e.g., Forward, Drop, Controller)

questions.justification: An OpenFlow table entry contains header match criteria, statistics counters, and matching actions.

questions.question: Why is centralizing control logic in an SDN Controller advantageous for urban-scale IoT deployments?

options.A: It provides global network visibility, enabling dynamic routing optimizations, global security enforcement, and automated traffic offloading
options.B: It eliminates the need for electricity
options.C: It limits network scaling to 10 nodes
options.D: It forces all data to be stored on paper

questions.justification: Global view allows SDN controllers to optimize flow placement, load balancing, and interference mitigation across urban IoT networks.

questions.question: Which OpenFlow switch software turns commercial wireless access points into OpenFlow-enabled switches running OpenWRT?

options.A: Pantou

questions.justification: Pantou turns commercial wireless routers/APs into OpenFlow switches using OpenWRT.

topics.description: Interference management, traffic offloading, SINR, and virtualized radio resource management.

questions.question: In Software-Defined Wireless Mobile Networks (SDWMN), how is inter-cell interference managed between neighboring eNodeBs?

options.A: The centralized SDN controller dynamically coordinates virtualized radio resource management (eICIC) across eNodeBs
options.B: By shutting down all cell towers
options.D: By using copper shielding between towers

questions.justification: Virtualized radio resource management under SDN control coordinates eNodeB transmit parameters to maximize SINR.

questions.question: What does ANDSF stand for in mobile traffic management under SDN architectures?

options.A: Access Network Discovery and Selection Function

questions.justification: ANDSF stands for Access Network Discovery and Selection Function.

questions.question: How does an SDN-based mobile gateway handle cellular traffic offloading to Wi-Fi?

options.A: The SDN controller dynamically installs flow rules steering heavy data streams from eNodeB to nearby Wi-Fi APs
options.B: By turning off cellular radios permanently
options.C: By converting cellular data to text SMS

questions.justification: SDN controllers install dynamic flow rules redirecting mobile data flows onto Wi-Fi networks when in range.

questions.question: What key formula defines Signal-to-Interference-plus-Noise Ratio (SINR) in mobile wireless networks?

options.A: SINR = Signal / (Interference + Noise)

questions.justification: SINR = S / (I + N), where S is desired signal power, I is interference power, and N is noise power.

questions.question: True or False: General OpenFlow natively supports mobile wireless networks without modifications.

options.A: False (General OpenFlow was designed for wired networks; modified versions like Odin/Mobi-Flow are required for wireless mobility)

questions.justification: Standard OpenFlow requires extension frameworks (like Odin, Ubi-Flow, Mobi-Flow) to handle wireless mobility and handoffs.

questions.question: Why is rule placement at access devices challenging in mobile IoT environments?

options.A: Users are mobile, creating dynamic topology changes that require frequent flow-table updates across heterogeneous access points
options.B: Flow tables can only hold 1 bit of data
options.C: Access points do not have power supplies
options.D: Wireless signals travel in straight lines only

questions.justification: Mobile devices move rapidly between APs, requiring frequent proactive or reactive flow-table modifications.

questions.question: How does Network Virtualization under SDN benefit heterogeneous mobile IoT users?

options.A: It abstracts physical hardware into virtual network slices tailored to specific service QoS requirements
options.C: It forces all devices to use the same speed

questions.justification: Network virtualization creates isolated software-defined slices with customized bandwidth and latency policies.

questions.question: In Software-Defined Wireless Mesh Networks, what is the primary role of Path Management?

options.A: Routing data based on application service requirements without depending on static core routing policies

questions.justification: SDN path management routes flows dynamically according to real-time delay, loss, or bandwidth constraints.

questions.question: How does centralized SDN control improve handoff latency when a mobile node moves between access points?

options.A: The controller pre-calculates the trajectory and proactively installs flow rules at the target AP before handoff completes
options.B: By dropping all data during handoff

questions.justification: Proactive rule placement by the controller eliminates setup latency during inter-AP handoffs.

questions.question: What parameter does Virtualized Radio Resource Management (vRRM) adjust in eNodeBs to maximize SINR?

options.A: Transmit power levels, subcarrier channel allocations, and beamforming parameters

questions.justification: vRRM coordinates radio transmit power, channel spectrum, and timing slots to minimize inter-cell interference.

topics.topic_name: Mobility-Aware Rule Placement Frameworks (Odin, Ubi-Flow, Mobi-Flow)
topics.description: Odin LVAP agent architecture, Ubi-Flow multi-controller partitioning, and Mobi-Flow predictive placement.

questions.question: Which architecture proposes placing an agent at access points to communicate with the controller as evaluated in Week 8 Question 1?

options.A: Odin

questions.justification: Odin proposes an agent-based solution placing an agent (Odin Agent) at access points.

questions.question: In Odin architecture, what virtual abstraction represents the client connection at the access point?

options.A: LVAP (Light Virtual Access Point)

questions.justification: Odin abstracts client Wi-Fi connections using Light Virtual Access Points (LVAPs).

questions.question: Which solution was proposed by the SWAN group for mobility-aware flow rule placement in mobile IoT systems as tested in Week 8 Question 2?

options.A: MobileFlow

questions.justification: MobileFlow was proposed by the SWAN group for mobile-based IoT networks.

questions.question: Which framework manages mobility in urban-scale software-defined IoT using network partitioning and flow scheduling?

options.A: Ubi-Flow

questions.justification: Ubi-Flow handles mobility management and flow scheduling in urban-scale software-defined IoT.

questions.question: Which framework uses proactive rule placement based on predicting user location at time (t+1) while at time (t)?

options.A: Mobi-Flow

questions.justification: Mobi-Flow predicts end-user location at time (t+1) to proactively place flow rules in target switches.

questions.question: How does Odin's LVAP (Light Virtual Access Point) enable seamless zero-hysteresis Wi-Fi handoffs?

options.A: The Odin Master moves the client's LVAP state from the old AP agent to the new AP agent without forcing the client to re-associate
options.B: The client reboots its Wi-Fi card
options.C: The user enters a new password

questions.justification: Moving the LVAP state between AP agents allows handoffs without client-side re-association overhead.

questions.question: What are the two core software components in the Odin architecture?

options.A: Odin Agent (placed on physical APs) and Odin Master (placed at the controller)

questions.justification: Odin consists of Odin Agents on access points and an Odin Master on the SDN controller.

questions.question: How does Ubi-Flow achieve fault tolerance and scalable control across urban-scale IoT access points?

options.A: By partitioning the urban network into distributed controller domains with multi-controller task-resource matching
options.B: By placing a single controller in a different country

questions.justification: Ubi-Flow uses multi-controller partitioning to distribute load and provide fault tolerance in urban networks.

questions.question: In Mobi-Flow, what happens to the flow tables on Base Stations (BS) and Access Points (AP) when a user moves from location t to t+1?

options.A: Flow rules for the mobile device are proactively updated on the target AP/BS before arrival, setting action to 'Forward'

questions.justification: Mobi-Flow pre-populates flow rules at the predicted target access device, ensuring continuous packet forwarding.

questions.question: Compare Odin, Ubi-Flow, and Mobi-Flow focus areas in Software-Defined IoT.

options.A: Odin focuses on WLAN LVAP agent abstraction; Ubi-Flow focuses on urban multi-controller scheduling; Mobi-Flow focuses on location-predictive flow rule placement
options.B: All three are optical fiber cabling standards
options.C: Odin is for cloud storage; Ubi-Flow is for Bluetooth; Mobi-Flow is for satellite

questions.justification: Odin abstracts WLAN APs; Ubi-Flow partitions urban multi-controller load; Mobi-Flow predicts mobility for proactive flow placement.
